nodes.name: Send to Telegram
nodes.notes: The menu keyboard is static: the node cannot vary its button count, and n8n drops an expression put in place of the fixedCollection. Format Message already builds the full reply_markup (a row per task, then the menu) for a raw sendMessage through an HTTP Request, which needs the bot token in a credential HTTP Request can use.

parameters.content:
## Daily Briefing

Sends calendar summary + price tracker + plugin sections every morning at 7 AM.

**Flow:** Schedule/Manual → Calendar → Price Check → Signups → Plugins → Format → Telegram

The SITE section is a plugin: the bot detector reads the `visits` table [15_site-visits](YOUR_GITHUB_REPO_URL/tree/main/projects/n8n/15_site-visits) writes.

Manual Trigger wired for testing.

## Button Callbacks
📊 briefing:expenses · 📚 briefing:learning · 🛍️ briefing:deals · 🗂 briefing:board · ❓ briefing:help
Tasks get no message of their own: tick them on 🗂 Kanban (`/board done <n>`) until the keyboard can carry a row per task.
Routed by menu-handler.json in [12_steward](YOUR_GITHUB_REPO_URL/tree/main/projects/n8n/12_steward)

## Standalone Briefing
Calendar + price tracker with inline action buttons.
Callbacks handled by menu-handler.json in project 10.

### Run Plugin — parameters

workflowId: ={{ $json.workflowId }}  (mode: id)
workflowInputs: none — the plugin trigger is
  set to passthrough, so the Plugins registry item
  (key, order, date, tz) IS the input.

n8n silently clears workflowInputs when a subworkflow
is re-selected. If a mapping reappears here, delete it.

onError = continueRegularOutput is load-bearing: a plugin
that throws must cost its own section, not the morning.
